items.summary_orig: Building a high-throughput webhook delivery engine means handling remote failures gracefully. When you deliver millions of webhooks a day to thousands of customer endpoints, naive retry loops, such as one exponential backoff schedule applied to every HTTP error, lead to worker starvation, retry storms and duplicated side effects.

items.title: 研究：长期孤独的消费者更少购买利他商品
items.title_orig: Lonely shoppers demonstrate less compassion in their purchases than others, study shows
items.summary: 康考迪亚大学等机构四项研究显示，长期孤独者较少购买公平贸易或无童工产品。

items.title: 如何用 FFmpeg 把 MOV 转 MP4：编码一致时直接流复制
items.title_orig: How to Convert MOV to MP4 With FFmpeg: Stream-Copy When the Codec Already Matches, and Re-Encode Only When It Doesn't
items.summary: 若视频已是 H.264、音频为 AAC，用 -c copy 重封装即可；ProRes、DNxHR 等需重新编码。
items.summary_orig: Short answer: to turn a QuickTime .mov into an .mp4 , start with -c copy . If the file is already H.264 video plus AAC audio, stream copy remuxes the packets, the first-frame RGB24 md5 stays the same, and the duration does not change. If the video is ProRes, DNxHR, or another codec that MP4 players will not handle, you have to re-encode.

items.title: 神经网络为何自信却出错，以及如何校准

items.summary_orig: A classifier that says it is 90% sure should be right about 90% of the time. That sounds like a low bar, and yet most modern neural networks fail it badly. They are routinely 99% confident and wrong, or 60% confident and right almost every time. Their accuracy can be excellent while their confidence is meaningless.

items.summary: 当像太阳这样的低质量恒星老化时，它们会离开主序并跟随红巨星分支。当它们上升到这个分支时，它们的亮度稳步增加。但路径中存在一种称为 RGB 亮度凹凸的小问题，它们的亮度会突然下降。
items.summary_orig: When low-mass stars like our Sun age, they leave the main sequence and follow the Red Giant Branch. As they ascend this branch, their luminosity steadily increases. But there's a sort of hiccup in the path called the RGB luminosity bump, where their luminosity suddenly dips.

items.summary_orig: For the second time in a few weeks, we’re writing about research into the temperature gap between the Sun’s surface and its corona. More and more data from various missions continue to feed this wave of discovery. A new paper by Katariina Nykyri of Embry-Riddle, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, adds to this growing body of work.
